extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing mathematics manuscripts for AMS-style journals (e.g., Journal of Algebra, Proc. AMS, Trans. AMS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for formatting a mathematics manuscript and its citations to conform to the American Mathematical Society (AMS) style, including top matter, running heads, end matter, pagination, lists, spacing, and reference formats for books and journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall writing principle
rubrics_metrics.description: “Less is more” in writing. Focus on accuracy and readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep prose concise and clear. Prioritize precise mathematical statements and readable exposition over verbosity. AMS Style represents best practices for presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallback grammar/style authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chicago Manual of Style is the guide used for grammar and style not covered by AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When AMS guidance is silent on a punctuation/grammar question, consult Chicago Manual of Style (17th ed. referenced). Specific Chicago sections are cited for pagination, spacing, grammar, and punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top matter required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Top matter (first page) should include: title, author line, abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required elements: title (with AMS capitalization rule), author line (initial and last name), abstract with heading. Some top-matter items related to journal publishing may be omitted in this handout but are covered in AMS Chapter 2 (pp.15–26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Title capitalization: Only first word, first word after colon, and proper names capitalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this capitalization scheme to the article title appearing in the top matter and running head (if used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author line format
rubrics_metrics.description: Author line should show initial and last name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use initials for given names and full last names in the byline (e.g., A. N. Other). Affiliations appear in end matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract heading and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract: list 'Abstract.' in bold, followed by description. 150 to 300 words, depending on length of paper. First-person pronouns are acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the heading exactly as 'Abstract.' (bold). Aim for 150–300 words; choose length appropriate to paper length. It's acceptable to use first-person pronouns in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running heads content and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Running heads on the right present the title (no longer than 50 characters / 4 inches); running heads on the left present the author’s name(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the title is longer than 50 characters, abbreviate it for the running head. If the author name(s) are long, shorten (use 'et al.' if too long). Acronyms may be used but do not use abbreviated words in running heads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running head abbreviation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Shorten long titles and long author lists: abbreviate title for right running head; use 'et al.' for long author lists on left running head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include abbreviated words in running heads. Acronyms are allowed. Ensure running heads remain readable and under the 50-character guideline for the title side.

rubrics_metrics.name: End matter elements
rubrics_metrics.description: End matter appears at the end and includes: acknowledgments, information about the author, references, author affiliations, author email and URL addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References are required. Acknowledgments and 'About the author' are optional. Include affiliation (department, university, location) as required; email and URL are optional. Use initials for first names when referring to individuals in acknowledgments and spell last names in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments format
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgements: Optional. References to individuals should include initials for first name and fully written last names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When acknowledging people, list them with initials and last names (e.g., A. B. Smith). Keep acknowledgments brief and relevant to the mathematics content.

rubrics_metrics.name: About the Author content
rubrics_metrics.description: About the Author: Optional. Brief description of title/status, university affiliation, membership, awards/prizes if related to the mathematics field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep biographical notes concise and relevant to the author's mathematical credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: References required and heading
rubrics_metrics.description: References: Required. The list of references follows the paper under the heading 'References.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a separate References section at the end of the manuscript with the heading 'References.' Ensure every in-text citation number corresponds to an entry here.

rubrics_metrics.name: References ordering and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: References should be listed in alphabetical order. Enumerate all references (they are end notes). Numbers in the references are NOT superscript. Indent from the number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alphabetize entries by author name. Prepend each entry with its reference number in brackets or plain numbers (not superscript); align/indent entry text after the number as shown in AMS examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal citations: Use reference numbers using brackets, e.g., [8], [11, Section 4.8], [3, 6, 7]. No page references are included in internal citations. Cite reference numbers directly rather than the author; authors may be named in the abstract but not in the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always use bracketed numeric citations for in-text citations. When citing a section within a reference, include the section after a comma in the brackets. Do not write author names in the body as substitutes for numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Books reference format
rubrics_metrics.description: Books: First Name Initial. [may write out name fully if available] Last Name, and First Initial. Last Name, Italicize book title: capitalize first letter of the first word and proper nouns, Volume number [if available], Publisher, Publisher’s City, Year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AMS book-entry examples (examples provided in the handout). Include series and volume numbers when applicable. Use italics for book titles and standard punctuation and ordering as in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal article reference format
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal: First initial or first name Last Name, Italicize title of journal article, Journal article [Capitalize, abbreviate, no italics]. Volume in bold (year), issue number, page numbers, DOI [space followed by number, no colon].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format journal titles as abbreviated (not italicized), put volume number in bold followed by year in parentheses, include issue and page range, and provide DOI with a leading space and no colon. See examples (e.g., J. Dumont ... IEEE Trans. Info. Theory. 56 (2010), no. 3, 1048-1069, DOI 10.1109/...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of MathSciNet for reference details
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS recommends using MathSciNet (MSC) database to identify how to use complete reference information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check MathSciNet entries for authoritative bibliographic data. Note that journals' reference styles in MathSciNet may differ slightly from the AMS examples on pp.65–66; use AMS formatting rules for the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pagination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Chicago Manual of Style 17th Edition format. All pages are counted in the pagination, regardless of whether numbers appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place page numbers generally at the upper right-hand corner of the page, one inch from the top and side. Number all pages (including tables and figures), starting with the title page. Arabic numbers may be used for front matter (Chicago Style, 2.38).

rubrics_metrics.name: List formatting and parallelism
rubrics_metrics.description: All phrases and all complete sentences should have parallel construction. Use 'stet' lists set within a paragraph if items are short (separate with semicolon). For longer lists, break out a single sentence and then indent the list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every list entry must be punctuated. Capitalize complete-sentence entries; phrases use lowercase. Do not use a colon after an introductory sentence if the list continues that sentence. Follow the handout's example formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line spacing and paragraph spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Line Spacing: Print outs should be double-spaced. Avoid extra space or blank lines between paragraphs (Chicago Style, 2.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use double spacing for manuscript drafts/printouts. Do not insert extra blank lines between paragraphs; rely on indentation or paragraph breaks per journal instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Space between paragraphs and colon: Single character space between sentences and after colons used within a sentence (Chicago Style, 2.9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single spaces between sentences and after colons inside sentences (i.e., do not use two spaces after periods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and punctuation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammar: See Chicago Style; Punctuation: See Chicago Style (specific page ranges given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For detailed rules on grammar (Chicago Style pp.225–362) and punctuation (pp.362–416), consult the Chicago Manual of Style as the authoritative source for items not explicitly covered by AMS guidance.
